manifest.name: dsh-macos-notifications
manifest.description: Native macOS Notification Center alerts for finished turns, approval requests, and agent questions — clicking a banner brings DeepSeek Harness to the front.

bundle.text:
# This bundle inserts one Host row. Install the package (or point the row at
# this directory) and keep the row enabled; see README.md.
- insert:
    - id: macos-notifications
      name: dsh-macos-notifications
      config:
        language: auto
        sound: Glass
        notifyOnTurnEnd: true
        notifyOnApproval: true
        notifyOnQuestion: true
        targetBundleId: com.deepseek.dsh
        openUrl: 'dsh://open'

readme.text:
A Host plugin for **DeepSeek Harness** that posts **native macOS notifications** through
Notification Center. Clicking a banner brings the Harness window to the front — the
same "take me back" behaviour the Dock-attention plugin gives its bouncing icon.

The plugin runs inside the Host process (the Node runtime behind the Desktop app),
watches the durable `session/event` feed, and hands every alert to a bundled native
helper, **DSH Notify**. It never writes to the session log and never talks to the model.

`osascript`'s `display notification` belongs to the script runner: the banner has no
app identity of its own, so clicking it can only focus the script editor (or reveal it
in Finder). The helper is a tiny `LSUIElement` app that posts the banner through
`UNUserNotificationCenter` under its own bundle id. macOS then routes the click back to
the helper, which activates DeepSeek Harness (or launches it, when it is not running)
and quits.

The helper is copied once to
`~/Library/Application Support/dsh-macos-notifications/DSH Notify.app` — quarantine
flag stripped, ad-hoc signed, registered with LaunchServices — and launched with
`open -n -g`, so posting a banner never steals focus and the notification permission
survives plugin updates. Request files and the helper log live next to it in
`runtime/`.

The banner wears the **DeepSeek Harness icon**: the banner shows the icon of the app
that posted it, so on install the plugin extracts `icon.icns` from the installed
Harness app, writes it into the helper bundle and signs it. Nothing third-party is
shipped in the repository; if Harness is not installed the configured
`targetBundleId` app's icon is used, and otherwise the generic app icon.

| Moment | Default | Notification |
|---|---|---|
| A turn finished | on | `Turn finished` / `Ход завершён` |
| A turn failed | on | `Turn failed` + the error message |
| A turn hit the token limit | on | `Token limit reached` |
| An approval is requested | on | `Approval needed · <tool>` |
| The agent asks a question (`ask_user_question`, `exit_plan_mode`) | on | `Your answer is needed · <question>` |

User-cancelled turns (`aborted`), forked and interrupted turns are silent. Subagent
sessions are ignored so only the sessions you actually see can ring the bell. The
notification body carries the session title (or, before a title exists, the workspace
folder name).
Every field is optional; the row's `config` mapping is merged over these defaults.

| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `language` | `auto` | `en`, `ru`, or `auto` (host locale). |
| `sound` | `Glass` | macOS system sound name or an absolute audio path; `null` for a silent banner. |
| `notifyOnTurnEnd` | `true` | Notify when a turn completes, fails, or is blocked. |
| `notifyOnApproval` | `true` | Notify when the agent waits for an approval decision. |
| `notifyOnQuestion` | `true` | Notify when the agent asks the user a question. |
| `targetBundleId` | `com.deepseek.dsh` | App a banner click activates. Point it at your browser's bundle id when you run `dsh web` in a browser. |
| `openUrl` | `dsh://open` | Opened by the helper when `targetBundleId` is not installed. |

The configured sound is played by the plugin itself while the banner stays silent, so
custom system sound names (`Glass`, `Ping`, …) keep working.

```yaml
- id: macos-notifications
  name: dsh-macos-notifications
  config:
    language: ru

The first banner triggers a system prompt — **"DSH Notify" Would Like to Send You
Notifications**. Click **Allow**, and the waiting banner is posted immediately. The
answer is cached per bundle id, so this happens once.

The helper waits up to two minutes for the answer; if you miss the prompt, open
**System Settings → Notifications → DSH Notify** and enable notifications. Without
permission no banners appear, and the helper log says
`authorization denied; the user must allow notifications for DSH Notify`.

**From GitHub (what the Plugins page manages).** Ask the agent to install the bundle, or
use the Plugins page with this spec:

```text
git+https://github.com/ihodorchenko/dsh-macos-notifications.git
```

To pin the release that introduced clickable banners:

```text
github:ihodorchenko/dsh-macos-notifications#v1.1.0
```

The `plugin_manager` tool takes the same spec as `install_bundle.target`. The bundle
patch inserts the `macos-notifications` row; the package carries its own
`dsh.bundle.patch`, locale metadata, and icon.

**From a local checkout.** Point `install_bundle` at the absolute package directory, or
pass `link:<absolute directory>` to the profile's package manager.

**Without Plugin Manager.** The Loader also accepts a plugin row that names a file URL
directly. Add this to `$DSH_HOME/profiles/desktop/cordis.patch.yml` (or your profile's
patch):

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: macos-notifications
      name: 'file:///absolute/path/to/dsh-macos-notifications/index.js'
      config:

Save the file while the app runs: the profile's HMR watcher recomposes the loaded
plugins, so a new row appears without restarting. A YAML error is rejected and the
previous configuration keeps running.

A `file:` row is not watched by HMR, because the file lives outside the profile
directory. After editing `index.js`, touch `cordis.patch.yml` or restart the app so the
module is imported again. Moving or deleting the checkout breaks a `file:` or `link:`
install; reinstall the bundle from the new path instead.

- **No banners at all** — check **System Settings → Notifications → DSH Notify**; the
  first run asks for permission and the answer is cached. The helper log lives at
  `~/Library/Application Support/dsh-macos-notifications/runtime/helper.log`.
- **Clicking a banner does nothing / opens Finder** — that is the pre-1.1.0
  `osascript` build (banners belong to the script runner). Update to 1.1.0+, where the
  banner belongs to DSH Notify and the click activates Harness.
- **Click activates the wrong app** — set `targetBundleId` (browser bundle id for
  `dsh web`) and restart the app.
- **No icon appears in the Dock** — by design: DSH Notify is an `LSUIElement` agent, it
  only exists to own banners and handle clicks.

```sh
node --test                        # 8 unit tests (config, sound, helper bundle, icon)
bash tools/build-helper.sh         # rebuild bin/DSH Notify.app (needs Xcode CLT)
node tools/self-check.mjs          # post a real banner and check the helper log
```

The helper source is small enough to audit: posting, the permission poll, and the
click/activation forwarding are all in `src/helper/main.swift`.

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `index.js` | Host plugin: session-event listeners, message rendering, helper install and launch |
| `bin/DSH Notify.app` | Native notification helper (universal binary, ad-hoc signed, `LSUIElement`) |
| `src/helper/main.swift` | Helper source; `tools/build-helper.sh` rebuilds the bundle |
| `tools/self-check.mjs` | Posts a real banner and reports the helper log tail |
| `~/Library/Application Support/dsh-macos-notifications/` | Installed helper copy, one-shot `runtime/requests/` and `runtime/helper.log` |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | Bundle patch that inserts the `macos-notifications` row |
| `locale/en.json`, `locale/ru.json` | Plugin Manager display metadata |
| `icon.svg` | Plugin icon |

MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE). The helper is ad-hoc signed (no Apple Developer identity),
so it carries no notarization; it is installed from the plugin package and needs no
quarantine escape hatch.
